Public surfaces must carry trust context (methodology, freshness, uncertainty) to maintain verifiability. Internal surfaces are operator-gated and must not leak protected logic. Protected surfaces encapsulate engine internals such as weights and thresholds, which are strictly isolated. The contract ensures that public exposure is bounded by configurable flags like canExposePublicPicks and canExposeEdgeIndex, which default to closed states. Failure modes include trust context omission, logic leakage, and unauthorized exposure. These invariants form a dual structure where public transparency is balanced against internal integrity. The system's robustness depends on enforcement of these boundaries through guardrails and telemetry.
